items.b: SILVER FELL 2.89% AND LED ALL FOUR METALS LOWER
items.t: Against this paper's 18 August marks of record, silver is down $1.88 to $63.12 and gold down $33.10 to $4,360.00, on Kitco at 05:58 New York and corroborated on TradingEconomics within 0.21%.

items.b: PLATINUM AND PALLADIUM COME OFF A THREE-SESSION HOLD
items.t: Both held marks, $1,749.00 and $1,311.00 from 17 August, sat above every live reading this morning. Both are retired and written at Kitco's $1,726.00 and $1,274.00, down 1.32% and 2.82%.

items.b: PALLADIUM'S TWO PAGES ARE 1.45% APART AND PLATINUM'S GAP IS A SETTLED BASIS
items.t: Kitco read palladium $1,274.00 against TradingEconomics at $1,292.50. Platinum's $11.90 gap is the sixth consecutive session of the same Kitco-low basis between 0.59% and 0.69%.

items.b: THE 30-YEAR TREASURY YIELD HIT ITS HIGHEST SINCE JUNE 2007
items.t: The long bond reached 5.31% and Japan's 10-year neared 3%, a three-decade high. Both second-page sources name the bond market rather than metals demand as the driver.

TradingEconomics has gold up 0.60% on the previous close, after a fall of nearly 2% during the 18 August session. This paper's 18 August mark was taken before that fall, so gold is $33.10 lower against it.

items.b: ROLEX IS SAID TO HAVE MADE DRAKE A PIECE UNIQUE, AND HAS PUBLISHED NOTHING
items.t: A gem-set Daytona announced on 16 August carries no reference, no stone count and no price. This desk found no statement from Rolex, and a claimed 2024 one-off undercuts the first-ever framing.

items.b: THE ONE PRICED WATCH IN THAT STORY MADE $500,000
items.t: A Drake-owned GMT-Master II, reference 116758SANR, sold through Wind Vintage earlier this year at the full ask after four offers, roughly five times average dealer value on EveryWatch data.

items.b: LAB-GROWN WHOLESALE IS DOWN 96% AND THE RETAIL MARKUP HAS NOT MOVED
items.t: The wholesale index fell 13% in the year to the second quarter and 26% across 2025. Retail markups still run above 80% over wholesale, one to two points from last year.

items.b: WHAT DID NOT PRINT TODAY, AND WHICH DESKS ARE DARK
items.t: Gemstones is dark an eighth consecutive edition, correctly, on its Tuesday and Friday cadence, with its next file due 21 August. Auctions is dark a second. Retail-tech is dark for the first time since 14 August. The Federation's July Swiss export print is due 20 August. The UAE gold intraday item was declined a sixth time.
